text: The open incident a grant is bound to is read through an IncidentStatusPort whose adapter is a Day-1 stub: the incident register's owner, store, contract and the incident reference pattern are fixed by no source of this read set, so the port is declared and stubbed rather than tied to a named system.
why: Legacy AC1 needs an open incident and AC2 a refusal when there is none, while FSD P4 v3 A2.28 names Log Analytics and the Workbench as the path and no incident store, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no incident path and no event.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1 and AC2 and section 5; FSD P4 v3 A2.28, AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-01; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 20; ownership map (no incident api row).
confirm: The security administrator and the platform on-call owner
impact: The grant is incident-bound from Day 1 and the check is a port, so the register can be named later with an adapter and no change to the rule, the criteria or the table.

text: The window in force is 4 hours from the activation, held as the parameter rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours and never as a constant; the code is this key's own and the value 4 hours is the value of the criteria and the tests.
why: Legacy AC1 says the system grants access for the window and fixes no length, FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 shows the activation at 10:30 and the grant active until 14:30, and no source names the parameter that carries the hours.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1 and AC3; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013; DP-06; Template and Rules R5.5.
confirm: The security administrator and the platform parameter owner
impact: A different window is a parameter row and no build; the four hours of the criteria stay the tested value.

text: The grant is held in break_glass_grant in rwb_access, named and shaped by this key as its own working decision: grant_id, actor_user_id, incident_reference, approval_reference, capability_area, right, scope, reason, starts_at, ends_at, state, ended_at, marker and the entry reference, with no BR Field ID and no ownership-map row.
why: No grant table exists in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and the ownership map has no row for one, while the criteria need a stored grant that the guard, the session read and the end operation read.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.0 and T3.1; ownership map tables list; legacy RWB-AD-006 section 11; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41.
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 1, 3, 11, 12.7, 13; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 11, 12.7; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 1, 2, 7, 8, 11, 12.7
confirm: The ACE database engineer and the data steward
impact: One table in the service's own schema, no cross-schema key, and a later official data-model entry is an additive change to the same table.

text: The end and read operations are this revision's decision at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}/end with right C and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId} with right R, idempotent by Idempotency-Key on the end, because no ownership-map row and no TSD row exists for either.
why: API-P4-013 publishes only the activation, the legacy Endpoints table gives only the access-log read that is not this story's, and Template and Rules R4 and DP-13 fix the base and the naming rule but not the paths.
read: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-013 only); ownership map api list; legacy RWB-AD-006 Endpoints and Permission checks; Template and Rules R4 and DP-13.
confirm: The solution architect and the security administrator
impact: The lifecycle is complete on Day 1 with three operations on one base, and a later TSD row can adopt the same paths without a consumer change.

text: No rwb.access event is published for a grant: the grant is session state and not a policy change, its readers are the authorisation guard, the breakGlass field of GET /me/session (API-P4-012) and the access-log marker of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, and the only message it produces is the library's decision-record entry.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43 give rwb-access exactly two business events, AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged, both for a cache refresh, and a grant that changes no permission row, no scope and no delegation limit would only cache an entitlement that has already expired.
read: Architecture v5 slides 11, 14, 20 and 43; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 (events: none); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-012 (session carries the break-glass state); DP-03 and DP-14.
confirm: The solution architect and the event platform owner
impact: One distributed state only, read on the call; no consumer subscribes to a name that does not exist and no cache holds an expired entitlement.

text: The clock is the authority over a grant: a grant is in force only while its state is ACTIVE and the time is before ends_at, the guard refuses every call after the window with no job and no person acting, and the row settles to ENDED with its AC-BGOFF entry on the next read, session read or authorised call; a grant nobody touches stays ACTIVE in its row and is out of force by time.
why: Legacy AC3 requires the grant to end with no action by anyone, and no source gives the service an expiry job or a Schedule: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives rwb-access only the six-monthly access review, so the window must be resolved on the read.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC3; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44; TSD P4 v3 T4; DP-17 (no scheduler in the service beyond the Schedule map).
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 4, 8, 9, 12.5, 12.6, 13; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 7, 8, 9, 12.5, 12.6; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 7, 8
confirm: The security administrator and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: No expiry job to lose and no job latency in the refusal; the cost is one UPDATE on the next read, and an untouched row still cannot be used as an entitlement.

text: The reason is at least 20 characters, the legacy floor, and at most 1000 characters, fixed by the column width and FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-02; the floor travels as a parameter (rwb.access.breakglass.reason-min) and is enforced both by the operation and by a check constraint.
why: Legacy AC1 fixes the minimum of 20 characters and says nothing of a maximum, FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-02 fixes the bounds as a validation rule, and no source names the parameter that carries the floor.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-02; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; DP-06.
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 14; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 7, 8, 11; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 7, 8, 11
confirm: The security administrator and the compliance officer
impact: A short reason is refused at the door and at the database, and a change of the floor is a parameter row and no build.

text: The retention of a grant is data: the retention class and the period are parameter rows of the parameters catalogue and never a literal in a migration, the table is not partitioned by this story, and the rollback of the migration drops the table, its constraints and its indexes only.
why: TSD P4 v3 T-B records DL26 as open for the retention periods, no source fixes a period for a grant, and a partition key would have to be chosen before the period is known.
read: TSD P4 v3 T-B (DL26 open); Architecture v5 slides 20 and 29; DP-15; DP-06.
confirm: The ACE database engineer and the compliance officer
impact: A period set at DL26 is a row, not a migration; the table carries no partition key it would later have to lose, and the rollback leaves the schema as the baseline found it.

text: The security administrator's approval is an IAM request outside the Workbench: the grant holds its reference as approval_reference and the approver reference beside it, the caller cannot approve the request it activates, and the Workbench runs no approval workflow of its own for a grant.
why: TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013 says the grant is approved in the bank IAM and activates it in the Workbench, FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-01 put the approval and the emergency group in the bank IAM, and Architecture v5 gives rwb-access no approval workflow.
read: TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013 and T6.1; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-01; Architecture v5 slide 14 (ApprovalWorkflow belongs to rwb-decision); legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1.
confirm: The security administrator and the bank IAM owner
impact: No second approval workflow is built, the four-eyes control stays where the bank already runs it, and the Workbench can always show who approved and when.

text: A person holds at most one active grant: the state values are ACTIVE, ENDED and REFUSED, and a unique partial index on actor_user_id where state = ACTIVE makes the database refuse a second active row for the same actor.
why: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-05 fixes the one-active-grant rule, the legacy story fixes no state vocabulary, and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines no grant table, so the states and the enforcement are this key's own.
read: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-05; legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.2; DP-15.
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 4, 5, 8, 9, 11; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 7, 8, 9, 11; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 7, 8, 11, 12.7
confirm: The security administrator and the ACE database engineer
impact: Two emergency windows cannot overlap for one person even under a race, and the state field has one vocabulary across the app, the contract and the schema.
